history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration expedite the process of defining and implementing the role of the Medical Services Division in technical supervision, oversight and enforcement of medical standards system- wide, based on the recommendations of the High- level Independent Panel on Peace Operations.
history.administration_response: An alternate proposal to establish technical supervision by a health- care practitioner registration mechanism is being drafted. A draft will be ready by mid-2022, but is expected to require considerable consultation, given that it has significant implications for the Medical Directors’ technical supervision dependencies. Regarding oversight of medical standards system-wide, in terms of the recommendations of the High- level Independent Panel on Peace Operations, the Health-Care Management and Occupational Safety and Health Division has standardized critical aspects of health-care quality management and patient safety by implementing common operational standards in all medical facilities in peacekeeping missions. This includes United Nations Health-care Quality and Patient Safety Standards manuals for level 1, level 1+, level 2 and level 3 facilities. The Division developed web-based training for hospital commanders and health-care workers in the field on the implementation of those standards in their health facilities in peacekeeping missions. Since 2020, the Division has trained 63 hospital commanders covering all hospital rotations. In addition, it has trained chief medical officers as assessors to evaluate implementation of standards in health facilities in field missions and referral hospitals. The self-sustained training and assessments of the compliance of health-care facilities will continue for years to come. The Administration requests the Board to consider the efforts taken to implement the recommendation and requests its closure.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Administration is currently drafting the role of the Medical Services Division, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration expedite the process of defining and implementing the role of the Medical Services Division in technical supervision, oversight and enforcement of medical standards system- wide, based on the recommendations of the High-level Independent Panel on Peace Operations.
history.administration_response: The request calls for clarification of the role of the Health-Care Management and Occupational Safety and Health Division in technical supervision, oversight and enforcement of medical standards system- wide. Given that the standards apply system-wide, they can only be implemented through mechanisms that apply to all medical entities that the Division supports. This has been achieved through the progressive introduction of a suite of new capabilities in the system- wide EarthMed record management system. These include technical clearances for all new medical staff, compulsory annual confidentiality agreements, compulsory standardized training requirements, clinical protocol audits, and a near real-time reporting dashboard for key medical processes. The Division’s authority is implemented through a comprehensive user access management system, where access by each individual user to the medical information system can be provided, modified or withdrawn. The request is therefore considered met and should be closed.
history.board_assessment: Given that the system wide technical supervision has been achieved, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
